conventions.hodgeTate: Hodge–Tate weights in the convention HT(Q_p(1)) = +1: h is a weight when Fil^{−h}D_dR ≠ Fil^{−h+1}D_dR (as in PadicHodgeTheory R06.2, R06.4, the L3–L4 packet and Lei–Loeffler–Zerbes). Sources with the opposite sign are translated.
conventions.periods: t = log[ε] for a fixed compatible system ε of p-power roots of unity; e_r = t^{−r} ⊗ ε^{⊗r} is the canonical basis of D_dR(Q_p(r)), independent of ε, with φ(e_r) = p^{−r}e_r; D_dR(Q_p(r)) is identified with K through e_r. In L2 only, the notation e_j inside D(T(j)), N(T(j)) and cocycles denotes the chosen representation basis ε^{⊗j}, not the canonical de Rham vector above; it scales by a^j when ε is replaced by ε^a.
conventions.frobenius: Arithmetic Frobenius throughout (φ(ζ) = ζ^p on roots of unity of order prime to p); sources using the geometric Frobenius (Huber–Kings 2003) are converted.
conventions.logarithm: The Iwasawa branch log_p(p) = 0 of ColemanIntegration:L0/iwasawa-logarithm; D_p(z) = Li_2(z) + ½ log_p(z) log_p(1 − z) is Coleman's D for this branch, equal to Besser–de Jeu's L_mod,2.
conventions.regulators: Soulé's étale regulator uses Chern classes; Besser's syntomic regulator reg_syn = η ∘ c^syn satisfies r^et = exp_BK ∘ reg_syn with no constant; D_p on completed K_3 is ε·log_BK ∘ c_{2,1} with the sign ε fixed by D_p([ζ]) = Li_2(ζ); Gros's normalisation is (1 − σ/p²)·D_p. For good-reduction curves, regP=Θ∘reg_syn=log_BK∘r_et and regSynCan=(1−Φ/q²)regP, with the explicit norm comparison β and transported K-action of D.5. Semistable curves have separate continuous reg^c,π and discrete reg^d coordinates; the symbol pairing is on ker N with a fixed uniformizer/branch. Relative AM Frobenius coordinates use a negative syntomic-coordinate comparison at n=1.
conventions.kTheory: K_3(L; Z_p) is π_3 of the p-completed K-theory spectrum (KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.1/completed-k-theory); for p > 3 and L unramified it is free of rank [L : Q_p] and equals the completion of Suslin's Bloch group.
conventions.cyclotomic: The LLZ source assumes odd p, uses HT(Q_p(1))=+1 and separates G=Delta times Gamma_1. R=Lambda_E(Gamma_1)=O_E[[X]][1/varpi], X=gamma-1, has bounded coefficients. It is not all of E[[X]]. The generic algebraic statements do not silently assume the source arithmetic hypotheses have been proved.
conventions.evaluation: Evaluation context: E is a field; R is a nonzero commutative E-algebra which is a domain; d,m are natural numbers; x:Fin m to E is injective; t is in R; ev_j:R to E are E-algebra homomorphisms with ev_j(t)=x_j. Each q_j=t-algebraMap(x_j) is NONZERO, and ev_j(f)=0 iff q_j divides f. J is a finite set of evaluation indices; V_j is an E-subspace of E^d. For the analytic application x_j belongs to the maximal ideal. Distinctness, the domain hypothesis and nonzero q_j are substantive, separate requirements.
conventions.matrices: Vectors of coefficients are rows; vectors of basis elements are columns. Domain basis n'=Un changes coordinates by U inverse. M maps bounded coordinates to analytic coordinates and changes by U M B inverse when the target basis changes by B. Apply the coefficient homomorphism to U where its ring differs from that of M.
conventions.determinants: Equality of principal determinant ideals is represented by association of nonzero generators; a basis does not choose a canonical scalar normalization.
conventions.integral: A nonzero determinant over O is not necessarily a unit. Constant O-integral basis changes preserve lattices. Finite-index integral image is weaker than surjectivity and rational surjectivity is weaker still.

summary: Construct the Chern-class-normalized p-adic regulators and their Bloch–Kato, syntomic and Coleman comparisons. For p>3 and finite unramified étale L/Q_p the completed local K₃ regulator is an isomorphism onto p²O_L and tame root classes generate its source. Construct the crystalline Iwasawa regulator, its conductor-sensitive interpolation and Wach-coordinate images, and the specified good-reduction, relative and semistable curve comparisons. The general-weight meromorphic target, source-restricted integral ranges and open global injectivity assertions are distinguished. The declarations are the two accepted part packets as they stand plus one node here; corrections to 31 imported targets (26 found by the first independent review, 5 locator slips by the second) are recorded as requests owed by those parts, not applied as an overlay.

nodes.title: Finite residue dilogarithm function
nodes.statement: For p prime and an F_p-algebra field F, define f_p(x)=li_{2,p}(x)/(x-1)^p on F^× minus {1}. Its total algebraic extension uses field inverse 0 inverse = 0, hence f_p(1)=0; this convention supplies no dilogarithm value or regulator class at the excluded root 1. For p>3 write li_{2,p}=(X-1)^2 g_p with deg g_p=p-3; then f_p(x)=g_p(x)/(x-1)^(p-2) for x≠1.
hypotheses: p prime; F a field over F_p. Root-count and spanning applications require p>3 and F finite.
proofSteps: Evaluate the finite polynomial and divide by the indicated power. On the admissible domain its denominator is a unit; cancel the double zero only when p>3 and x≠1.

uses.how: Bound each fibre on the q-2 admissible points by p-2, then span by values and differences.
Identify the reduction of p^-2 D(zeta^p) with f_p(zeta bar).

tests.statement: For admissible tame zeta, p^-2 D(zeta^p) mod p equals f_p(zeta bar), with arithmetic Frobenius on the argument.

fields.title: Good Wach basis coordinate interface
fields.statement: Import rational and analytic good-basis existence from PG.6/wach-good-basis; PG.6 owns this generic theorem. The stronger integral choice n_i congruent n_i^0 modulo pi of LLZWach2010 Theorem 3.5 is an extension requested from PG.6. For the selected good basis identify its bounded coefficient row with Lambda_E(G)^d and its analytic extension with H_E(G)^d, using b_i=(1+pi)phi(n_i). A constant invertible change of the selected Wach basis changes the coefficient row by inverse right multiplication. A change of basis by a matrix in GL_d(Lambda_E(G)) with non-constant entries transforms the coordinates as in L4/constant-basis-covariance with R=Lambda_E(G); it need not carry a good basis to a good basis.
proofSteps: Use the imported basis and analytic scalar-extension theorems under their weight and topology hypotheses. The stronger integral prescribed-reduction result is LLZWach2010 Theorem 3.5, pp.10–12, and belongs to the PG.6 extension request.

Expand uniquely in b_i. Constant basis change acts identically on the column of b_i, so the coefficient row multiplies by its inverse. This is the regulator coordinate interface, not another Wach existence construction.

fields.statement: For K/Q_p finite and V de Rham, the dual exponential exp*_{K,V^*(1)} : H^1(K, V) → Fil^0 D_dR(V) is the composite H^1(K, V) → H^1(K, B_dR ⊗ V) ≅ D_dR(V), the isomorphism being x ↦ (g ↦ log χ(g)·x) (Kato); its image lies in Fil^0 D_dR(V) and its kernel is H^1_g(K, V). For W=V*(1), write P_W:H^1(K,W)×H^1(K,W*(1))→Q_p for the ordered cup-product pairing, and Q_W:D_dR(W)×D_dR(W*(1))→Q_p for its de Rham pairing followed by trace. The adjunction is Q_W(x,exp*_{K,W}(y))=P_W(exp_{K,W}(x),y), with x∈D_dR(W)/Fil^0 and y∈H^1(K,V), identifying W*(1)=V. Reversing both pairings requires the corresponding graded-commutativity sign; their order is part of the convention. This is the positive adjunction of LZ2014 §2.4, not a choice of Iwasawa normalization. The proof of LZ2014 Theorem B.6 writes both pairings with the W*(1) argument first; translating between the two orders multiplies by the sign −1 of the degree-one cup product, unless the transposed Tate pairing is defined without that sign.

fields.statement: Throughout PadicHodgeRegulators: (i) t = log[ε] ∈ B_dR^+ is the period of Z_p(1) for a fixed compatible system ε = (ζ_{p^n}) of p-power roots of unity; Fil^i B_dR = t^i B_dR^+, g(t) = χ(g)t for the cyclotomic character χ, and φ(t) = pt in B_cris (arithmetic Frobenius). (ii) Hodge–Tate weights: h is a weight of V when Fil^{−h}D_dR(V) ≠ Fil^{−h+1}D_dR(V); with this convention Q_p(1) has weight +1 and V_pA of an abelian variety has weights 0 and 1, matching the L3–L4 conventions, PadicHodgeTheory R06.4 and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.3 (HT(χ) = +1). (iii) For r ∈ Z, e_r := t^{−r} ⊗ ε^{⊗r} is a basis of D_cris(Q_p(r)) = K_0·e_r and of D_dR(Q_p(r)) = K·e_r, independent of ε, with φ(e_r) = p^{−r}e_r, Fil^{−r} = D_dR and Fil^{−r+1} = 0; hence D_dR(Q_p(r))/Fil^0 = K·e_r for r ≥ 1 and 0 for r ≤ 0. (iv) Twisting: D_cris(V(i)) = D_cris(V)⟨i⟩ via d ↦ d ⊗ e_i, with Fil^j(D⟨i⟩) = Fil^{j+i}D and φ|_{D⟨i⟩} = p^{−i}φ|_D. (v) Crystalline representations have N = 0; the monodromy operator is used only for semistable inputs (D.5's boundary). Sources using the opposite weight sign (Benois: Q_p(1) of weight −1) are translated, never mixed.
